q1.text: When a sudden crisis occurs where a major client complains about your team's work, what is your first instinct?

options.leadership: Gather the team to immediately divide emergency handling tasks.
options.detail: Analyze data logs and previous reports to find the exact location of the error.
options.creativity: Think of creative compensation or additional services to calm the client.
options.execution: Immediately call the client and solve the technical problem right then and there.

q2.text: If you are asked to lead a new product launch project, what part do you enjoy most?

options.creativity: Designing product concepts and branding strategies that have never existed before.
options.execution: Ensuring the timeline runs fast and weekly targets are achieved without excuses.
options.detail: Developing detailed SOPs and checking QA (Quality Assurance) before release.
options.leadership: Motivating team members across divisions so the product vision is aligned.

q3.text: Your colleague is on leave and you have to back up their work which contains hundreds of lines of spreadsheet data. Your reaction?

options.detail: Great. I love tidying up and making sure the numbers are accurate.
options.leadership: I will delegate some parts to other staff to be more efficient.
options.execution: I will do it as fast as possible so today's target is still completed.
options.creativity: I will try to create new formulas/macros to make the format more attractive and easy to read.

q4.text: In an annual evaluation meeting, your communication style is usually...

options.execution: Focus on action items to be executed immediately tomorrow.
options.creativity: Giving wild ideas about the company's future direction.
options.leadership: Directing the discussion so all team members get a chance to speak.
options.detail: Bringing complete notes about achieved/failed metrics and KPIs.

q5.text: What is the biggest weakness that you (or others) often realize in yourself?

options.execution: Often ignoring small rules to achieve goals quickly.
options.detail: Too perfectionist on small things so sometimes slow.
options.creativity: Often jumping from one idea to another before the first one is finished.
options.leadership: Too much taking over work because of lack of patience seeing a slow team.
